paragraphs.source_en: My master, who had gone out with Mr. Kangetsu, wandered off somewhere, heaven knows where. He did not come home until late that night, and the next morning it was already past nine when he appeared for breakfast. As usual I watched him from atop the rice tub; he silently ate his ozoni, bowl after bowl. The pieces of rice cake were not large, but still, he ate six or seven of them. At last he left one piece in the bowl, put down his chopsticks, and said, Well, no more. If anyone else had casually left food in a bowl, he would never have stood for it; yet he, swelling with self-satisfaction in the dignity of household headship, gazed quite unconcernedly at the charred corpse of rice cake soaking in the cloudy broth. His wife took some stomach powder from the cupboard and set it on the table. At this my master said, That medicine does no good. I will not take it. But dear, they say it is very effective for starchy foods. You really ought to take it. She kept urging him to swallow it. My master lapsed again into his obstinate habit and said, Starch or no starch, it is useless. I will not take it. You really are fickle, his wife muttered. I am not fickle. The medicine simply does not work. But only the other day you were saying how wonderfully it worked, and you took it every single day, did you not? My master replied in a tone like a balanced couplet: Then it worked; now it does not. If you take it for a while and stop for a while like that, even the most effective medicine is sure not to work. A weak stomach is not like other illnesses; unless you patiently keep taking medicine, it will never get better. As she said this, she glanced back at Osan, who stood waiting with a square tray in her hands. Osan at once took the mistress's side without condition, saying, Sir, madam speaks the truth. Unless you keep taking it for a few more doses, how can you tell whether it is good medicine or bad? Good or bad, I say I will not take it, so I will not take it. What do women know? Hold your tongue. His wife said, After all, we are only women. As she spoke, she pushed the stomach powder toward him, trying to force him to drink it down. My master, however, rose without a word and went into his study. His wife and Osan looked at each other and broke into a sly little laugh. At such times, if I followed close behind my master and sat on his knees, I would come in for a dreadful experience; so I went around through the garden, climbed onto the veranda before the study, and peeped in through a gap in the paper screen. There was my master, reading a book by someone called Epictetus. If he could understand that book as he ordinarily pretended to, then he would indeed have something admirable about him. But after five or six minutes he flung the book down onto the desk as if striking it there. I had expected something of the sort all along. Watching carefully still, I saw that this time he took out his diary and wrote the following entry:

paragraphs.source_zh: 同寒月君一同出去的主人，也不知他们上哪儿散步去了。直到当天晚上很晚才回来，第二天出来吃早饭已是九点多钟了。我照例在饭桶上看着主人，他一声不响地在吃煮年糕，吃了一碗又一碗。尽管年糕片不很大，但他毕竟吃了六七块啊。最后把一块剩在碗里，放下了筷子说道：“咳，不吃啦。”如果是别人随便把吃的剩在碗里，他是决不答应的，但是，摆出一家之长的架子而自鸣得意的他，看着浸在浓汤里焦烂的年糕残骸，却丝毫不以为然。主人妻子从壁橱里拿出胃散，放在桌子上。于是主人说道：“这个药不管用，我不吃！”“怎么你……人家说这对淀粉食物很管用呢，还是吃了好啊！”她一个劲儿劝他吃。主人又犯了他那执拗的毛病，说道：“什么对淀粉管用不管用的，不吃！”妻子嘟囔说：“你这个人真是没常性！”“不是我没常性，是因为药不管用。”“你前些日子不是说真管用，真管用，每天都在吃吗？”主人使用对句似的口吻说道：“彼时管用，此时不管用啦。”“像你那样吃一阵停一阵，就是多管用的药也保险不会管用的。胃病不同于别的病，不耐心吃药，是不会好的呀。”她说着回头看了看端着方盆等候在那里的阿三。阿三立刻无条件地站在女主人一边，说道：“老爷，太太说的是实话，您要不继续吃几顿看，怎么能知道它是好药还是坏药呢。”“不管它好坏，我说不吃就是不吃。女人家懂得什么，少多嘴！”主人的妻子说道：“反正我们是女人。”说着把胃散推向主人，想强制他喝下去。主人却一言不发地站起来，走进了书斋。主人的妻子和阿三面面相觑，嘻嘻地笑了起来。这种时候，如果我紧跟在主人后边，坐到他的膝上，就会大吃苦头，所以我从院子绕过去，爬到书斋前的廊子里，从纸窗的间隙往里偷偷一瞧，主人正摊开爱比克泰德写的书在读着哩。如果他能像平时那样读懂这本书，当然很了不起。可没过五六分钟，他就把书本狠狠地扔在书桌上。我早就料到会有这一手。留心看下去，这次他拿出日记本写下了如下的记事：

paragraphs.source_en: Walked with Kangetsu around Nezu, Ueno, Ikenohata, and Kanda. In front of a trysting house at Ikenohata, geisha in spring kimono with colored flowers embroidered along the hems were playing battledore and shuttlecock. Their dress was beautiful, but their faces were ugly, rather like our cat at home.

units.source_en: Walked with Kangetsu around Nezu, Ueno, Ikenohata, and Kanda.
units.source_zh: 与寒月去根津、上野、池之端、神田一带散步。

units.source_en: In front of a trysting house at Ikenohata, geisha in spring kimono with colored flowers embroidered along the hems were playing battledore and shuttlecock. Their dress was beautiful, but their faces were ugly, rather like our cat at home.

paragraphs.source_en: There was no need to drag me in specially as an example of ugliness. Even I, if I went to Kita's barbershop and had my face shaved, would not be so very different from a human being. The trouble with humans is that they are so conceited. My master's diary then continued:

paragraphs.source_zh: 大可不必为说明其面孔丑陋，特地把我当作例子呀。即便是我，只要到“喜多美容店”去刮刮脸，不见得会比人差多少。糟糕的是，人总是这样自高自大。主人的日记接着写下去：

paragraphs.source_en: As we turned the corner by the Hotan drugstore, another geisha came along. This geisha was slender, with sloping shoulders, and very prettily made; the pale purple clothes she wore suited her naturally and looked refined. Showing her white teeth as she smiled, she said, Gen-chan, about last night, well... I was just terribly busy. However, her voice was as hoarse as a crow's cry, greatly diminishing the charm of her graceful appearance. I could not be bothered to turn around and see what sort of person this so-called Gen-chan might be, so with my hands tucked in my sleeves I went straight out onto Onari Road. Kangetsu, for some reason, seemed rather restless and beside himself.

paragraphs.source_zh: 拐过“宝丹”药铺房角，又走来一个艺妓。这个艺妓身材苗条，柳肩，长得很俊俏，身上穿着浅紫色衣服，很合体，看起来很雅致。她露出雪白的牙齿笑着说道：“小源哥，昨儿晚上嘛……实在是我太忙啦。”不过她那声音嘶哑得和乌鸦叫一样，使她那风流俊俏的姿态大为减色。我懒得回头去看所谓小源哥究竟是何许人，便甩着双手径直来到“御成路”。寒月不知为什么，似乎有些魂不守舍的样子。
